title: Console content-aware stacking and compact-mode behavior for charts, tables, and modals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) degrade on small viewports and across browsers when density controls are applied. Charts can clip or repaint poorly, table columns overflow or hide important metrics, and modals lose anchor relationships (scroll jumping, off-screen stacking). This ticket designs a content-aware stacking and compact-mode strategy that preserves key information, maintains touch/keyboard affordances, and reduces cross-browser layout regressions.

Scope: produce high-fidelity prototypes and interaction specs for: compact/dense display mode, table column compression rules (priority-based truncation), chart canvas fallbacks (svg/static snapshot at narrow widths), modal anchoring & stacking context rules, and guidelines for safe component-level min-width/min-height and interaction hit areas. Prepare cross-browser acceptance criteria and a short QA checklist for engineering and design reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Compact-mode UI shows a stable, prioritized information hierarchy at 320px–480px widths without horizontal scroll
Table compression uses priority metadata to collapse secondary columns into a drilldown or ellipsis popover; primary columns remain visible
Charts switch to low-overhead snapshot rendering or simplified sparkline at narrow widths to avoid canvas repaint flicker on Safari/Firefox
Modal stacking rules prevent content from appearing offscreen and maintain keyboard focus order when multiple overlays are present
Touch targets meet 44px minimum in compact mode; keyboard navigation and focus outlines remain visible
Cross-browser verification performed on latest Chrome, Safari (macOS+iOS), Firefox, and Edge with documented bugs and workarounds
comments: 2026-02-20 Asha: Kicked off initial exploration. Two approaches sketched: (A) progressive compression where elements gradually reduce padding/line-height and hide lower-priority columns; (B) content clipping where charts/tables are clipped and replaced with a compact summary. Leaning toward progressive compression for readability.

2026-02-26 Miguel Torres (ENG): Flagged a Chrome-specific canvas repainting flicker when switching chart types during resize; engineering suggests snapshot fallback for narrow widths to avoid GPU thrash.

2026-03-02 Design Review: Team preferred priority-based column collapse and modal anchor rules that pin to viewport edge when anchor is offscreen. Requested accessibility notes for keyboard flow and announced values for hit area sizes.

2026-03-05 QA notes from Zoe (PM): Add test cases for cost table row density toggle and ensure totals row never hides. Also requested a microcopy suggestion for the density toggle to clarify behavior.
2026-03-11 Lina: Prototype v2 uploaded with compressed typography scale, updated spacing tokens, and an SVG fallback for line charts. Shared with ENG for feasibility review.
decision_log: 2026-02-24 Decision: Adopt progressive compression as primary strategy; fall back to clip+summary only when compression would hide >40% of primary metrics.
2026-03-03 Decision: Use snapshot SVG fallback for charts at widths <= 360px on Safari to avoid canvas repaint and subpixel rounding issues.
2026-03-08 Decision: Modal stacking will use an explicit z-index layer with 'modal-anchor' translation; if anchor is offscreen, modal pins to top 12px of viewport to maintain context.
risks: Different browser rendering of subpixel rounding could cause minor layout shifts — mitigated by integer-based spacing tokens and 1px tolerance in QA
Aggressive compression may reduce discoverability of secondary metrics — mitigated by drilldown and inline summaries
Performance cost of swapping renderers (canvas<>svg) — engineering to implement lightweight snapshot and cache strategy
next_steps: Finalize Figma prototypes and export annotated spec by 2026-03-16
Pair with ENG (Miguel, Priya) to validate chart fallback approach and table compression implementation by 2026-03-19
Create a QA checklist and run cross-browser exploratory session, log findings in Confluence page
Ship a small design tokens change (spacing/line-height) behind feature flag to test compact-mode in staging
